Existing producers this slice consumes unchanged: utils/restore_readiness.py (RB.0), utils/recovery_manifest.py, utils/recovery_validation.py (RB.4 V1-V3 verdicts), utils/recovery_retention.py, data/state/recovery_attestations.json (RB.3a).

context_not_loaded: Any device contact, credential, or recovery payload bytes -- this slice renders manifests/readiness only (section 11), never payload, never a download link, never a decrypt path
RB.3b's watched real R81.x run -- separate, hardware-gated, Product-Owner-run
invariants: Section 6 rule 1: no payload bytes, no download URL, no decrypt affordance, ever -- a test greps the rendered HTML for artifact bytes / digests-of-payload and must find none (contracts 9.3)
Section 6 rule 2: restore_proven renders as an explicit badge; the unqualified word 'verified' never appears in the module
Section 6 rule 3: available:false renders an explicit empty state, never a silent blank module

Section 5 rules 1-3 are consumed, not re-derived: held_artifacts and attested_not_held are never merged; READY requires a held artifact at >= V3 AND version_matches_running; inventory device with no record is UNPROTECTED, UNKNOWN only when inventory itself is insufficient

The recovery_ui builder is a pure function over persisted state (readiness record + manifests + validation + retention) -- no rendering concerns inside it -- so UI 2.0 can call the same projection later
AGENTS.md: adding the module obliges a tests/fixtures/uitest/ extension and a green render harness

report.objective: Implement RB.5 -- the last unbuilt slice of project/backlog.json id native_backup's RB.0-RB.5 line: readiness scoring roll-up and the Recovery UI module, per docs/design/BACKUP_AND_RECOVERY_ARCHITECTURE.md section 11 and docs/design/BACKUP_RECOVERY_CONTRACTS.md section 6 (`recovery_ui` payload, frozen rules 1-4). RB.4 (validation battery V1-V3) is AUTOMATED_VALIDATED, so RB.5's stated gate ('after RB.4') is satisfied. The core deliverable is the `recovery_ui` PROJECTION -- a persisted, value-free posture payload built from the RB.0 readiness record, held manifests, validation levels and retention state; the static HTML Recovery module renders that projection. Product Owner context 2026-09-09: this projection is exactly the kind of 'persisted projection both surfaces read' that the upcoming UI 2.0 (separate shell, Java, PostgreSQL) will consume -- so the payload builder must be a clean, standalone function over persisted state, not logic buried in the HTML renderer.
output_contract: A recovery_ui payload builder (e.g. utils/recovery_ui.py or the existing *_ui.py builder pattern's home) producing exactly the section 6 shape: available, generated_at, readiness_summary, coverage {devices_in_inventory, devices_with_any_artifact, coverage_percent}, devices[].artifacts[] {class, age_days, validation_level, restore_proven}, retention_pending_deletion[]

The Recovery module rendered from that payload (readiness roll-up, per-device timeline with validation level shown per artifact, coverage-vs-inventory gap view, retention view), injected via the same mechanism as configuration_ui / crypto_ui / discovery_ui, plus the single Overview recovery-posture tile
compliance_posture: readiness exposed as an additive evidence source (no new control yet -- section 11 says 'for a future backup-coverage control')
tests/fixtures/uitest/ extended with a recovery fixture covering READY / STALE / PARTIAL / UNPROTECTED / UNKNOWN and available:false; render harness green

Tests for section 6 rules 1-4 and contracts 9.3 (no payload bytes in HTML), 9.7 (restore_proven:true without restore_proof rejected -- if the validator does not already enforce it, do not weaken it) and the empty state
project/backlog.json native_backup note + BACKUP_AND_RECOVERY_ARCHITECTURE.md status line / section 12 table updated: RB.5 AUTOMATED_VALIDATED; build_history record

risks: Rendering any artifact digest, name, or payload-derived bytes 'for traceability' -- forbidden by section 6 rule 1 / contracts 9.3
Burying projection logic in the HTML renderer so UI 2.0 cannot reuse it
